findings.title: Enrollment revoke uses bare confirm() instead of ConfirmDialog
findings.description: handleRevokeEnrollment uses native window.confirm() for a destructive action (revoking an enrollment code that cannot be undone). All other destructive actions in the codebase were migrated to ConfirmDialog in STBT-186.1, but this one was missed. Native confirm() is not style-consistent, cannot be themed for dark mode, and provides a poor UX.
findings.code_snippet: if (!confirm(`Revoke enrollment code ${code}? This cannot be undone.`)) return;
findings.recommendation: Replace with showConfirm() pattern like confirmedBulkFF, confirmedApproveProduct, etc.
findings.production_impact: UX inconsistency on enrollment revocation; no theming; blocks the main thread
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.003 covers bare confirm() for feature kill switch, R5.SA.004 covers staff deactivation, R5.SA.012 covers GRN alert actions. This enrollment revoke is a distinct case not covered by any existing ticket.

findings.title: StaffTab deactivate button uses inline confirm() bypassing confirmed wrapper
findings.description: The Deactivate button in StaffTab.tsx has an inline confirm() guard: `if (s.is_active && !confirm(...)) return; handleToggleStaffActive(s.id, s.is_active);` However, App.tsx already wraps handleToggleStaffActive with confirmedToggleStaffActive (line 2599-2603) which shows a proper ConfirmDialog. The StaffTab receives confirmedToggleStaffActive as the handleToggleStaffActive prop. This means a staff deactivation triggers BOTH a native confirm() AND then a ConfirmDialog -- double confirmation for the same action.
findings.code_snippet: onClick={() => { if (s.is_active && !confirm(`Deactivate staff member "${s.name}"?`)) return; handleToggleStaffActive(s.id, s.is_active); }}
findings.recommendation: Remove the inline confirm() from StaffTab.tsx since the parent already wraps with ConfirmDialog.
findings.production_impact: Users see two confirmation dialogs in sequence for staff deactivation. Confusing UX.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.004 describes 'staff deactivation uses bare confirm instead of ConfirmDialog' but the fix in STBT-186.1 added a ConfirmDialog wrapper in App.tsx WITHOUT removing the original confirm() in StaffTab.tsx. This finding is about the DOUBLE confirmation, not the missing confirmation.

findings.title: Resend welcome message uses native alert() instead of structured feedback
findings.description: handleResendCode uses native alert() to display the resend result: `alert('Welcome message resent...')`. This blocks the main thread, is not themed, and does not match the ConfirmDialog/toast pattern used everywhere else in the app.
findings.code_snippet: alert(`Welcome message resent${result.sentTo ? ` to ${result.sentTo}` : ""} via ${result.channels.join(", ")}`);
findings.recommendation: Replace with toast notification (Toaster is already configured) or use a result modal similar to EnrollmentResultModal.
findings.production_impact: Blocks main thread. UX inconsistency with rest of app.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers alert() in handleResendCode. R5.SA.004 and STBT-186 only cover confirm() dialogs.

findings.title: AIInsightsTab storeId passed in URL without encodeURIComponent
findings.description: The AIInsightsTab passes storeId directly into URL query string without encoding: `/api/v1/admin/ai/anomalies?storeId=${storeId}&limit=50`. If a storeId contains special characters (e.g., &, =, #), this could break the URL parsing or allow parameter injection.
findings.code_snippet: const result = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/admin/ai/anomalies?storeId=${storeId}&limit=50`);
findings.recommendation: Use encodeURIComponent(storeId) or URLSearchParams for query string construction, consistent with how other API modules do it (e.g., devices.ts uses new URL() with searchParams).
findings.production_impact: Query parameter injection risk if storeId contains special characters. Could return wrong data or cause API errors.
findings.dedupe_note: LIVE.SA.AI_PROMPT_INJECTION_GUARD covers the AI question field prompt injection. This is a different issue -- storeId URL encoding in anomalies/alerts endpoints.

findings.title: AIInsightsTab job endpoints use unvalidated path construction
findings.description: The runJob function constructs endpoint URLs from hardcoded strings passed through the template: `/api/v1/${endpoint}`. While currently the endpoint values are hardcoded in the JSX, the function signature accepts any string. If the endpoint array were ever modified to include user input, this would be a path traversal risk. More immediately, the endpoint paths use 'admin/jobs/*' without the leading 'admin/' in some, creating inconsistency with the established '/api/v1/admin/' prefix pattern.
findings.code_snippet: const result = await apiFetch(`/api/v1/${endpoint}`, { method: 'POST' });
findings.recommendation: Use a fixed base path: `/api/v1/admin/jobs/${jobName}` with jobName from a whitelist enum.
findings.production_impact: Low immediate risk (values are hardcoded), but fragile pattern. If extended, could hit wrong endpoints.
findings.dedupe_note: LIVE.SA.AI_ENDPOINT_PREFIX_PARITY covers AI health/ask endpoint prefix consistency. This is about the job trigger endpoints in AIInsightsTab, not the AI Q&A endpoints.

findings.title: useNavigationSafety hooks defined but never imported or used
findings.description: The useNavigationSafety.ts file defines two hooks: useUnsavedChanges (beforeunload guard) and useDraftStorage (sessionStorage with TTL). Neither hook is imported or used anywhere in the codebase. The app has its own beforeunload logic inline in App.tsx. This is dead code that creates confusion about the intended architecture.
findings.code_snippet:
export function useUnsavedChanges(isDirty: boolean) { ... }
export function useDraftStorage<T>(key: string, defaultValue: T, ttlMs = 300000) { ... }
findings.recommendation: Either remove the unused file or integrate the hooks into the corresponding features (App.tsx beforeunload, product edit modal draft persistence).
findings.production_impact: Dead code. No functional impact but adds confusion for maintainers.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers this dead code.

findings.title: Events tab Prev button not disabled on first page
findings.description: The Prev button in EventsTab is never disabled. Clicking Prev on page 0 will set page to 0 (via Math.max(0, p - 1)) but the button remains visually clickable, which is poor UX. Compare with other tabs (DevicesTab line 314, AuditTab line 134, DocumentsTab line 87) which properly disable their Prev buttons when on page 0.
findings.code_snippet:
<button className="tab" onClick={() => setPage((p) => Math.max(0, p - 1))}>
  Prev
</button>
findings.recommendation: Add `disabled={page === 0}` to the Prev button.
findings.production_impact: Minor UX issue -- button appears clickable but does nothing on first page.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.011 covers 'Prev/Next pagination buttons never disabled' but refers to store directory pagination in StoresTab. This is a separate instance in EventsTab.

findings.title: Mobile navigation tab bar missing 4 tabs present in sidebar
findings.description: The mobile fallback tab bar (line 2834-2858) is missing the 'grn-alerts' tab name display. It shows 'GRN' (line 2848) but this is actually present. However, comparing sidebar (23 buttons for 23 tabs + AI panel) with the mobile nav (23 buttons), the mobile nav does NOT include the 'quality' tab with the label 'Quality' but DOES include it on line 2853. After careful line-by-line comparison: the sidebar lists 'quality' between 'monitoring' and 'credit-providers', and mobile nav also has it. Actually on closer look the count matches. But the labels differ: sidebar says 'Finance' for credit-providers (line 2752) while mobile says 'Finance' too (line 2854). The real issue is the sidebar has 'AI Intelligence' (line 2758) but mobile has just 'AI' (line 2856) -- inconsistent labels could confuse users switching between views.
findings.code_snippet:
sidebar: 'AI Intelligence'
mobile: 'AI'
findings.recommendation: Standardize tab labels between sidebar and mobile navigation. Consider using a shared TAB_LABELS constant.
findings.production_impact: Minor UX inconsistency. Users on mobile see abbreviated labels that don't match sidebar.
findings.dedupe_note: LIVE.SUPERADMIN.MOBILE_NAVIGATION covers mobile navigation issues broadly. This specific label inconsistency is a distinct net-new finding.

findings.title: SupportQueueTab resolve action fires without confirmation dialog
findings.description: The resolveConversation function fires directly on button click without any confirmation. Resolving a support conversation closes it permanently. The 'Assign to Me' action on line 127 also fires without confirmation. These are destructive/irreversible actions that should follow the ConfirmDialog pattern used in the rest of the app.
findings.code_snippet: <button onClick={() => resolveConversation(selectedConvId)} ... >Resolve</button>
findings.recommendation: Add ConfirmDialog before resolving or assigning conversations.
findings.production_impact: Accidental clicks can resolve support conversations prematurely. No undo mechanism.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers SupportQueueTab action confirmations. R5.SA.001/002/003/004/012 cover other tabs' missing confirmations but not support queue.

findings.title: SupportQueueTab selectConversation silently swallows all errors
findings.description: When loading conversation messages fails, the catch block silently sets messages to empty array without any error feedback: `catch { setMessages([]); }`. The user sees an empty chat with no indication that loading failed.
findings.recommendation: Set an error state and display it in the chat area so the user knows messages failed to load.
findings.production_impact: If message loading fails (network error, auth expired), user sees empty chat with no indication of failure.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.007 covers tab-switch error clearing, not error swallowing. This is a distinct error handling gap.

findings.title: SupportQueueTab reply input allows raw Enter-key submission without Shift+Enter for newline
findings.description: The reply input sends the message on plain Enter keypress. There is no way to type multi-line messages since Enter always sends. For admin support replies, this can lead to incomplete messages being sent accidentally.
findings.code_snippet: onKeyDown={e => e.key === 'Enter' && sendReply()}
findings.recommendation: Use a textarea instead of input, and only send on Enter (not Shift+Enter). Or add Shift+Enter for newline: `e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey && sendReply()`.
findings.production_impact: Admin cannot send multi-line support replies. Accidental partial message sends.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers this input behavior.

findings.title: GstComplianceTab catch blocks use err:any pattern without sanitization
findings.description: Multiple catch blocks use `catch (err: any)` and display `err.message` directly without sanitization: lines 30, 45, 62. The GST API module (gstCompliance.ts) throws errors with raw HTTP status codes like 'GST summary failed: 500' which could expose internal server information.
findings.recommendation: Use parseError/sanitizeErrorMessage from errorSanitizer.ts, or update the GST API module to sanitize errors before throwing.
findings.production_impact: Internal error details (HTTP status codes, server error messages) may be displayed to admin users.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.021 covers 'catch err:any pattern' as a general pattern issue. This finding is specifically about the GST tab's unsanitized error display combined with the raw HTTP status error messages from gstCompliance.ts.

findings.title: Monitoring API triggerTokenCleanup leaks raw HTTP status in error message
findings.description: The triggerTokenCleanup function throws `new Error('Token cleanup failed: ${res.status}')` which exposes the raw HTTP status code. This is inconsistent with other API modules that use parseError/sanitizeErrorMessage from errorSanitizer.ts.
findings.code_snippet: if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Token cleanup failed: ${res.status}`);
findings.recommendation: Use parseError from errorSanitizer.ts: `throw new Error(await parseError(res));`
findings.production_impact: Low -- admin-facing only. But inconsistent error handling pattern.
findings.dedupe_note: LIVE.SA.INVOICE_API_ERROR_SANITIZATION covers invoice API error sanitization. This is the monitoring API, a distinct module.

findings.title: Invoice API error messages expose raw HTTP status codes without sanitization
findings.description: Multiple functions in invoices.ts throw errors with raw HTTP status: 'Failed to list invoices: 500', 'Failed to get invoice: 404', etc. (lines 156, 165, 176, 187, 198, 209, 219, 228, 237, 248). Unlike analytics.ts which uses the centralized sanitizeErrorMessage, invoices.ts exposes raw status codes.
findings.code_snippet: if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Failed to list invoices: ${res.status}`);
findings.recommendation: Use parseError from errorSanitizer.ts for all error throws.
findings.production_impact: Internal HTTP status codes displayed to users in error messages.
findings.dedupe_note: LIVE.SA.INVOICE_API_ERROR_SANITIZATION.001 exists but its description says 'Invoice API error messages expose internal details'. Checking the current code, this is still present (not fixed), so this may be a confirmation rather than net-new. However, LIVE.SA.INVOICE_API_PATH_SANITIZATION is about path sanitization not error sanitization. Including as potential overlap -- reviewer should check if LIVE.SA.INVOICE_API_ERROR_SANITIZATION was implemented.

findings.title: DocumentsTab blob URL leaked on re-selection without cleanup
findings.description: The useEffect cleanup for blob URLs (line 63) references blobUrl from the closure, but blobUrl is stale because it references the value at the time the effect was created, not the current value. When the user selects a different document, the previous blob URL may not be revoked because the cleanup function captures the old blobUrl. Additionally, the eslint-disable comment on line 66 explicitly suppresses the exhaustive-deps warning that would catch this bug.
findings.recommendation: Use a ref to track the current blob URL, or revoke in the effect body before creating a new one.
findings.production_impact: Memory leak from unrevoked blob URLs when reviewing multiple documents in sequence.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.019 covers 'blob URL cleanup has stale closure' in App.tsx barcode sheet download. This is a DIFFERENT stale closure in DocumentsTab's document preview blob URL -- distinct file, distinct feature.

findings.title: ApplicationsTab entity filter change uses setTimeout instead of useEffect for refresh
findings.description: When changing the entity filter, a setTimeout(50ms) is used to trigger refreshApplications: `onChange={(e) => { setAppEntityFilter(e.target.value); setTimeout(() => refreshApplications(), 50); }}`. This is a race condition -- the refresh may fire before the state update has propagated, fetching with the old filter value.
findings.code_snippet: onChange={(e) => { setAppEntityFilter(e.target.value); setTimeout(() => refreshApplications(), 50); }}
findings.recommendation: Use a useEffect in App.tsx that watches appEntityFilter and triggers refresh, or pass the new filter value directly to the refresh function.
findings.production_impact: Race condition: filter change may not take effect on refresh, showing stale data.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers this specific race condition pattern.

findings.title: GstComplianceTab GSTR-1 export blob URL not revoked in error path
findings.description: The handleExport function creates a blob URL with createObjectURL, clicks a link to download, then revokes. However, if the user navigates away or the download fails silently, the a.click() may not trigger the download and the blob URL is revoked immediately after click. The a element is also never appended to the DOM (unlike App.tsx line 2222-2225 which properly appends/removes). Some browsers require the element to be in the DOM for click() to work.
findings.recommendation: Append the anchor to document.body before clicking, then remove it, consistent with App.tsx's handleBarcodeSheetDownload pattern.
findings.production_impact: GSTR-1 export download may silently fail in some browsers (Safari requires DOM attachment).
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.023 covers 'GSTR export uses programmatic click pattern' but focuses on the click pattern itself. This finding is about the missing DOM attachment which makes the pattern fail in certain browsers.

findings.title: AuditTab CSV export only exports current page, not all filtered results
findings.description: The 'Export CSV' button exports only auditLogs (the current page of 50 records), not all filtered audit logs. The button tooltip says 'Export current page as CSV' which is accurate, but there is no way to export all audit logs matching the current filter. For compliance purposes, admins may need full audit trail exports.
findings.code_snippet: <button onClick={() => exportAuditCsv(auditLogs)} ... title="Export current page as CSV">Export CSV</button>
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Export All' option that fetches all pages server-side and exports, or note the limitation clearly.
findings.production_impact: Admins cannot export full audit trail for compliance review. Limited to 50 records per export.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers this audit export limitation.

findings.title: WhatsAppTab broadcast recipient count not validated against server-side max
findings.description: The WhatsAppTab UI enforces a max of 50 recipients for broadcast (visible in the tab code), but this limit is only enforced client-side in the textarea parsing. If the server has a different limit, there is no server-side validation feedback. The whatsapp.ts API module does not validate the phones array length before sending.
findings.code_snippet: N/A -- conceptual: client enforces 50 max but server may differ
findings.recommendation: Add server-side limit validation in whatsapp.ts or display the server's actual limit.
findings.production_impact: Low -- the 50-recipient limit is reasonable and currently enforced client-side.
findings.dedupe_note: LIVE.SA.WHATSAPP_PHONE_VALIDATION covers phone number format validation. This is about broadcast recipient count limits, a different concern.

findings.title: AI panel ask button catch uses err:any and does not sanitize error message
findings.description: The AI ask button's catch block casts error as `any` and displays the raw error message: `setAiError(e?.message ? String(e.message) : 'AI request failed')`. The ai.ts API module may return server error details that should be sanitized before display.
findings.recommendation: Use sanitizeErrorMessage from errorSanitizer.ts before displaying, or ensure ai.ts sanitizes all thrown errors.
findings.production_impact: Server error details could be displayed in the AI panel error message.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.021 covers the general 'catch err:any' pattern. LIVE.SA.AI_PROMPT_INJECTION_GUARD covers prompt injection. This is specifically about the AI panel's error display without sanitization.

findings.title: ErrorBoundary does not reset state -- requires page reload
findings.description: The ErrorBoundary component catches errors but only offers 'Refresh Page' and 'Go Home' buttons. There is no 'Try Again' option that resets the error state and re-renders children. This means any React rendering error forces a full page reload, losing all in-memory state including auth session.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Try Again' button that calls `this.setState({ hasError: false, error: null })` to attempt re-rendering.
findings.production_impact: Any React error forces full page reload, losing admin session context.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers ErrorBoundary recovery behavior.

findings.title: Registration events polled on every 60s interval regardless of current tab
findings.description: In the 60-second polling interval, refreshRegEvents is always called (line ~1866: `r.refreshRegEvents?.()`) regardless of which tab the user is on. This means registration events are fetched every 60 seconds even when the user is on the Events, Analytics, or any other tab. While this is intentional (to update the sidebar badge count), it creates unnecessary API load. Other tab-specific data is only fetched when the user is on that tab.
findings.code_snippet: // In polling interval: r.refreshRegEvents?.() called regardless of tab
findings.recommendation: Consider only polling registration events when the badge needs updating (i.e., when not on the registrations tab) and reduce the frequency, or use server-sent events / WebSocket for real-time badge updates.
findings.production_impact: Unnecessary API calls every 60 seconds for all admin users, increasing backend load.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.026 covers 'auto-refresh interval does not reset when switching tabs'. This is about always-on polling for a specific resource, a different concern.

findings.title: Refunds API module uses inconsistent base URL pattern
findings.description: The refunds.ts API module defines a base() function that returns `API_BASE || ''` (line 31-33), creating an extra function indirection that other modules (e.g., whatsapp.ts, analytics.ts) do not use. More importantly, it constructs query strings manually (`?${qs.toString()}`) when the value might be empty, potentially appending a bare '?' to the URL.
findings.code_snippet:
const qStr = qs.toString() ? `?${qs.toString()}` : "";
const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${base()}/api/v1/admin/refunds${qStr}`, {
findings.recommendation: Standardize on the pattern used in analytics.ts (getJson helper) or use URLSearchParams consistently.
findings.production_impact: Low -- works correctly but inconsistent patterns increase maintenance burden.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers API module pattern inconsistency for refunds specifically.

findings.title: DocumentsTab review modal has dark background that contradicts light theme
findings.description: The document review modal uses hardcoded dark colors: `backgroundColor: '#1a1a2e'` (line 134) and `backgroundColor: '#0f0f23'` (line 146) for the document preview area. This creates a jarring visual when the rest of the app uses light theme. The modal is not using theme variables (var(--color-bg), etc.) and will not adapt to the theme toggle.
findings.code_snippet:
<div style={{ backgroundColor: "#1a1a2e", borderRadius: 8, padding: 24, ... }}>
...
<div style={{ ... backgroundColor: "#0f0f23", padding: 16, ... }}>
findings.recommendation: Use theme CSS variables instead of hardcoded dark colors, or at minimum use the standard modal classes (modalOverlay, modal) that are theme-aware.
findings.production_impact: Visual inconsistency: document review modal is dark regardless of theme setting. Poor accessibility contrast.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers DocumentsTab modal theming.

findings.title: CreditProvidersTab uses parseInt on potentially floating-point statistics
findings.description: The CreditProvidersTab aggregates provider health statistics using parseInt() on string values returned from the API. If the API returns floating-point numbers as strings (e.g., '3.5' for average response time), parseInt will truncate to '3', losing precision. This could result in inaccurate summary card values.
findings.code_snippet: parseInt() used for stats aggregation in CreditProvidersTab
findings.recommendation: Use Number() or parseFloat() instead of parseInt() for numeric statistics.
findings.production_impact: Summary statistics may be truncated, showing inaccurate totals.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers this numeric parsing issue.

findings.title: Approval result modal in ApplicationsTab not keyboard-dismissable
findings.description: The approval result modal (shown after approving a store application) at line 3141 does not handle Escape key to dismiss. It only closes when the 'Done' button is clicked. Other modals in the app (ConfirmDialog, ConfirmationModals) dismiss on backdrop click and some handle Escape. This modal also has no backdrop click handler to dismiss.
findings.code_snippet:
<div style={{ position: 'fixed', inset: 0, background: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.5)', ... }}>
  ... <button onClick={() => setApprovalResult(null)}>Done</button>
findings.recommendation: Add onClick on the backdrop to dismiss, and add onKeyDown Escape handler.
findings.production_impact: Minor UX -- admin must click Done button to dismiss; cannot use Escape or backdrop click.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers this modal's keyboard/backdrop interaction.

findings.title: Clipboard writeText calls silently swallow errors without fallback
findings.description: Multiple clipboard operations use navigator.clipboard?.writeText().catch(() => undefined) which silently swallows errors. If the clipboard API is not available (HTTP context, permissions denied), the user gets no feedback that the copy failed. Found in: DevicesTab lines 119-121 (copy code), 129-131 (copy QR payload), App.tsx line 3161 (copy activation code), ConfirmDialog line 64 (copy enrollment code).
findings.code_snippet: navigator.clipboard?.writeText(enrollment.code).catch(() => undefined);
findings.recommendation: Show a toast notification on success, and show an error toast or fallback (select + document.execCommand) on failure.
findings.production_impact: Users click 'Copy' buttons with no feedback on whether the copy succeeded or failed.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.SA.022 covers 'document.execCommand copy used which is deprecated'. This is the opposite problem -- the newer clipboard API is used but errors are silently swallowed with no user feedback.

findings.title: Events tab CSV export includes all filtered events but no progress indicator for large exports
findings.description: The 'Export CSV' button on the Events tab calls exportCsv(filteredEvents) which processes all events synchronously. For the maximum of 1000 events, this could cause a brief UI freeze. There is no loading state or progress indicator.
findings.code_snippet: <button onClick={() => exportCsv(filteredEvents)}>Export CSV</button>
findings.recommendation: Add a loading state while generating CSV, or use a Web Worker for large datasets.
findings.production_impact: Brief UI freeze possible with 1000 events. Minor.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers events CSV export performance.

findings.title: Quality API resetMetrics has no confirmation of what was reset in response
findings.description: The resetMetrics function is a destructive POST that returns void. The QualityDashboardTab shows no success confirmation after reset -- it just reloads data. The user has no way to confirm the reset actually happened other than seeing zeroed metrics.
findings.recommendation: Return a result from the API (e.g., `{ reset: true, timestamp: ... }`) and show a success toast.
findings.production_impact: Low -- admin gets no explicit confirmation that metrics were reset.
findings.dedupe_note: No existing ticket covers this quality metrics reset feedback.
